00_n: Hello, Miles! I'm Eva, your English teacher. Today we read Animals' Weather. We will look, read, think, and talk. Are you ready? Let's go!
01_n: Miles, this is our lesson map. There are four parts. Today we do part 1 and part 2. Next time we do part 3 and part 4. You can tap a number at the top to jump.
02_n: Miles, look at this picture. What do you see? Start with: I see. Then say: I think. Then say: I wonder. Tap Record and talk. Tap Continue when you finish.
02_rn: Here are some ideas. I see a dog with an umbrella. I think it will rain. I wonder, how does the dog know? Great wondering, Miles! Tap Continue.
03_n: Turn to page 10. The book says: The weather changes often. It can be sunny one day and rainy the next. People use technology to guess the weather. But animals can guess the weather, too.
04_n: Here is today's big question. How can animals guess the weather? Miles, make a guess. Say it out loud. Start with: Maybe animals...
04_rn: Good guess, Miles! Remember your guess. We will read the story, and then we will check it.
05_n: Let's meet six new words. Say them with me and do the actions. Neck. Touch your neck. Air. Breathe in the air. Rabbit. Hop like a rabbit. Fat. Make a big tummy. Know. I know! When. When will it rain?
06_n: Stretch. Stretch means to make your body long. Look, the cat stretches. Miles, stand up and stretch your neck and arms. Stretch!
07_n: Smell. We smell with our nose. She is smelling a flower. Miles, use your nose. Smell the air!
08_n: Now turn to page 11. Look at the words and listen. Farmers need to know about the weather. Their farms need it! Animals can help.
09_n: Cows and horses know when it will rain. They stretch their necks. They smell the air. Then the farmer knows it will rain.
10_n: Winter is coming. The rabbits are eating a lot. They are getting very fat. Then the farmer knows it will be a long, cold winter. How do the animals know?
11_n: Let's echo, Miles. Listen to me first. Cows and horses know when it will rain. Now it's your turn. Tap Record and say it just like me.
11_rn: Listen again. Cows and horses know when it will rain. Tap Play to hear yourself. Do you sound the same? Tap Continue.
12_n: One more. Listen. The rabbits are eating a lot. They are getting very fat. Your turn, Miles. Tap Record and say it.
12_rn: Listen again. The rabbits are eating a lot. They are getting very fat. Tap Play to hear yourself. Well done! Tap Continue.
13_n: Miles, be a detective. How does the farmer know it will rain? Look at the story. Tap the sentence that tells you.
13_rn: They smell the air. The cows and horses smell the air, so the farmer knows it will rain. Check page 11.
14_n: One more, detective. How does the farmer know winter will be long and cold? Tap the sentence that tells you.
14_rn: They are getting very fat. Fat rabbits tell the farmer it will be a long, cold winter. Check page 11.
15_n: Remember your guess, Miles? How can animals guess the weather? Now you know more. Was your guess right? Tell me.
15_rn: The story says animals use their bodies. Cows and horses stretch their necks and smell the air. Rabbits eat a lot and get fat. Good checking!
16_n: The story ends with a question. How do the animals know? Miles, what do you think? Start with: Maybe...
16_rn: The book does not give an answer. That's OK! Maybe animals can feel or smell the air change. But maybe is not the same as a fact. How could we check, Miles? Look at the last line on page 11.
17_n: Now retell the story, Miles. Use these helpers: First. Then. So. Tap Record and tell me the story. Tap Continue when you finish.
17_rn: Here is one way to say it. First, cows and horses smell the air. Then, the rabbits get very fat. So, animals help farmers. Tap Continue when you are ready.
18_n: Session 1 is finished, Miles. You looked, guessed, read, and checked your guess. You found proof in the story, too. Next time we find the main idea and think like a scientist. Bye bye!
19_n: Hello again, Miles! Today we do part 3, main idea and details, and part 4, use it and think more. Tap a number if you want to jump.
20_n: First, remember the story. Turn to page 11. Cows and horses know when it will rain. The rabbits get very fat before a long, cold winter.
21_n: Today we learn two important words: main idea, and details. The main idea is what the whole story is about. Not one little line. The big idea for the whole page.
22_n: A detail is one little fact in the story. Details help the main idea. They are little facts that hold up the big idea.
23_n: I will read a sentence from the story. Is it the main idea, or a detail? The rabbits get very fat. Tap the one you think is right.
23_rn: Detail! The rabbits get fat. That is one little fact. Check the chart on page 12.
24_n: Next sentence. Animals can help farmers know about the weather. Is it the main idea, or a detail? Tap one.
24_rn: Main idea! The whole story is about animals helping farmers know about the weather. Check question 1 on page 12.
25_n: Look at this table, Miles. The table top is the main idea: animals can help farmers know about the weather. The legs are the details. A table needs legs to stand. A main idea needs details to hold it up.
26_n: Miles, think. Which little facts in the story are the legs of this table? Say them out loud.
26_rn: They stretch their necks. They smell the air. They eat a lot. They get very fat. Four legs found! Check the chart on page 12.
27_n: Listen to this sentence from the book. Cows and horses know when it will rain. We can use know when to talk about us, too. I know when it is lunchtime. My dog knows when I come home.
28_n: Your turn, Miles. Make your own sentence. Start with: I know when. Tap Record and say it.
28_rn: Here are some more. I know when it is bedtime. I know when Dad is home. I know when it will rain, because the sky is dark! Tap Continue.
29_n: Turn to page 13. Tap the correct word for each line, Miles.
29_rn: When. Necks. Smell. Did you get them right? Check page 13.
30_n: Open your book to page 13. The project is called Weather and Animals. We sort sentences into two groups: It will rain, and it will be a long, cold winter.
31_n: Here are four sentences from the book. A. The rabbits are getting very fat. B. The cows and horses smell the air. C. The rabbits are eating a lot. D. The cows and horses stretch their necks. Ready to sort?
32_n: Think carefully, Miles. Which sentences go with rain? Which go with a long, cold winter? Drag each card to the right box.
32_rn: Here is the sort. It will rain: the cows and horses smell the air, and stretch their necks. Long, cold winter: the rabbits are getting very fat, and eating a lot. Check page 13.
33_n: Now let's think like a scientist. A fact is always true. A saying is something people say. It may be true, or not. Fat rabbits mean a long, cold winter. Is it a fact, or a farmer's saying? Tap one.
33_rn: It's a farmer's saying. It may be true, but not always. Maybe the rabbits are just hungry, or there is lots of food. Asking, is it always true, is critical thinking!
34_n: Miles, how could we check if it is true? What could a scientist do? Tell me one idea.
34_rn: Here are some ideas. Watch the rabbits. Write it down. Then see if the winter is long. Scientists watch, write, and check. Great thinking!
35_n: Now you are the teacher, Miles! Teach Mum or Dad the story. Use the sentences on the screen. Speak clearly, and answer their question. Tap Record if you want, and tap Continue when you finish.
35_rn: Great teaching, Miles! Animals can help farmers. Cows and horses smell the air before rain. Rabbits get very fat before a long, cold winter. Tap Continue.
36_n: Here is a mission for today, Miles. Look outside. Is it sunny, or cloudy? Will it rain? Watch the birds, cats, or ants. Do they do something before the rain? Tell Mum or Dad what you see.
37_n: Today you found the main idea and the details. You made your own sentence with know when. You asked, is it a fact or a saying, and you taught the story. That is critical thinking and communication. Great job, Miles. Bye bye!
